title: Growth rate is interrupted at physiological epochs such as birth, puberty, metamorphosis

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Growth rate is interrupted at physiological epochs such as birth, puberty, metamorphosis

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Curves of growth show well-marked interruptions or changes of rate at physiological epochs such as birth and puberty, in man and in other animals, and most strikingly in animals that undergo a regular metamorphosis.

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Ch. III: The Rate of Growth

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: Just as the human curve of growth has its slight but well-marked interruptions, or variations in rate, coinciding with such epochs as birth and puberty, so is it with other animals, and this phenomenon is particularly striking in the case of animals which undergo a regular metamorphosis.

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci On Growth and Form claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: D’Arcy Wentworth Thompson, On Growth and Form (1st ed., Cambridge: Cambridge University Press, 1917), Chapter III, “The Rate of Growth”; topic “Growth epochs and metamorphosis”. Scope: animals, including man, mouse, silkworm, tadpole

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on thompson1917-ch03-14: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.73

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Change-point analysis gives a direct test and rich human data cover birth and adolescence. Existing open data can test selected metamorphosing taxa, but not the broad assertion across animals.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Fit segmented growth curves around independently dated birth, puberty and metamorphic transitions and test for discontinuities or slope changes. Smooth trajectories through those epochs would refute the corresponding component.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Puberty and metamorphosis timing must be measured independently of growth.

Comparable longitudinal mass or size series are sparse outside model species.

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Interruptions at named physiological epochs can be looked for in human growth surveys and in compiled animal life cycles. The human adolescent case is well powered; birth and, especially, metamorphosis depend on scattered series, and a slope change at an epoch that coincides with a change of habitat is only partly discriminating. The general claim is therefore testable in pieces.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Test for a change in the slope of growth rate at birth and at puberty in humans, and at metamorphosis in insects, amphibians, and other transforming animals. Marked slope changes at those epochs, strongest where metamorphosis is regular, would support the claim; smooth velocity through them would count against it.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Metamorphic growth series are not gathered as a single designed dataset.

Human birth and puberty effects are modest and easy to confuse with a change of environment or measurement.
